business_problem: Shopee needed large language models that could handle multilingual ecommerce tasks across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, and Brazil, but general-purpose frontier models degraded sharply on regional languages, shopping concepts, fraud workflows, and customer-service use cases.
solution_summary: Shopee built its own ecommerce LLM stack, centered on the Compass family of models, on top of NVIDIA AI Factory infrastructure. The company pretrained Compass-v3 as a 245B-parameter mixture-of-experts model on 12 trillion tokens of curated multilingual corpora and synthetic ecommerce instructions, using NVIDIA Megatron-Core for distributed pretraining across NVIDIA A100, H100, and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU fleets. In post-training, Shopee uses NVIDIA NeMo for instruction tuning, preference alignment, and agentic reinforcement learning methods such as OTPO and SPEC-RL. NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM then serves Compass models in production across search, recommendations, fraud detection, customer service, and logistics. This gives Shopee one domain-built platform that connects large-scale training, multilingual alignment, and production inference for regional commerce workloads.

data_flow: Shopee curates multilingual ecommerce corpora and proprietary marketplace data into the Compass training pipeline, Megatron-Core and NeMo produce aligned domain models on large GPU fleets, TensorRT-LLM serves those models in production, and the outputs feed search, recommendations, fraud, logistics, and customer-service experiences across regional markets.
business_outcome: Shopee scaled Compass API usage from 3 billion to 340 billion monthly tokens in eight months, delivered 50x faster fraud detection at 90 percent lower cost, outperformed frontier models on regional ecommerce benchmarks, and expanded AI across conversion, ads, logistics, and multilingual customer interactions.
